# Final overhead campaign (2026-09-09) — Generated by Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic)

The campaign the paper's overhead numbers come from. Run as one driver
(`scripts/campaign_final_20260909.sh`), 00:23 → 13:29, **no failures except one
run** (see below).

## Configuration — identical for both halves

| | |
|---|---|
| host | `scripts/host_perf_mode.sh split`: **SMT off**, **turbo off**, performance governor, thermald stopped |
| application | P-cores `0,2,4,6,8,10` (`FISH_APP_CPUS`) |
| observer | E-cores `12-17` (`FISH_OBS_CPUS`) — LTTng daemons, FISH daemon, probes |
| desktop | E-cores `18-19` (user slice `AllowedCPUs`) |
| instrumentation | `per_instance = true` → `ros2:rcl_publish` + `ros2:rmw_take` (filter `taken == 1`) |
| nsys | lean profile (`python/fish/nsys_flags.py`) |
| thread pool | **stock** — no `FISH_NPROC` shim (proven irrelevant, see `notes/campaign_np6_2026-09-08.md`) |
| thermal | throttle counters 0/0 at start and at end, TCPU 47 → 49 °C |

Why SMT off: with the application pinned to the six primary threads, an enabled
SMT would leave the sibling threads free of *measured* work (container cpuset
excludes them, the desktop slice excludes them) — but `system.slice` and kernel
threads are unconfined, so the sibling could still take work and cost the
application a fraction of its core. Small, but unquantified. SMT off makes that
term exactly zero.

**Why this campaign supersedes the earlier ones:** until now the Autoware runs
had `per_instance = true` and the Isaac sweep had it `false`, so the two
overhead tables measured *different* instrumentation and their percentages were
not comparable. They now measure the same thing. The Isaac sweep also ran with
the pre-lean nsys profile before this.

noise narrowing rather than a change in the system.

The three-mode form (base / lttng / nsys, with CPU) is in `summary.md` +
`summary.csv` in the campaign directory.

**unet now has all three nsys repetitions** (`fish_20260909_104655 / _105455 /
_110255`, ~684 MB each, sqlite exported) — in the 09-06 sweep two of the three
had failed, so the paper's unet figures were still coming from the unpinned
2026-08-30 session. These sessions replace it, and they carry the same
instrumentation as the Autoware ones.

### The one failure

`dnn_image_encoder lttng #3 rc=124` (the run's own timeout, not the watchdog).
Base and nsys have 3/3, so the base-vs-FISH table above is unaffected; only the
lttng column of that bench rests on two repetitions. Re-run it alone if that
column is used.

### Things to read carefully before quoting

* `bi3d` base fps ±3.3 and `dope` jitter ±37 are genuine run-to-run spread, not
  measurement error — the delta for those benches is inside the noise.
* `stereo_image_proc` FISH jitter 1.35±1.35 ms is one repetition out of three
  being far off; the other two sit at the baseline. Same for `visual_slam`
  (±4.6) and `unet` (±4.1).
* The Isaac numbers are now *higher* cost than the 09-06 sweep for the jitter
  metrics, which is expected: `per_instance = true` adds the per-message
  publish/take events that the earlier Isaac runs did not record.
